items.title: Chance The Rapper Celebrates Birth of Third Daughter, Hayli: ‘Mom n Dad Love You’
items.summary:
Chance the Rapper is a girl dad three times over. The “No Problem” MC announced in an Instagram post on Sunday (Nov. 15) that he recently welcomed his third daughter, Hayli. “Welcome to the world Hayli,” he wrote in the caption. “Mom n Dad love you. God is with you.”

The accompanying slideshow featured images of an unidentified woman snuggling with the newborn in the hospital, as well as snaps of the hip-hop star with his hand on her very pregnant belly and another in which he painted a carved pumpkin image on his partner’s stomach (“Hayli’s first Halloween costume”) and some of the “nesting” prep for the family’s new addition; the post did not detail when and where the child was born.

Chance, 33, (born Chancelor Bennett) did not identify the woman in the photos. He shares two older daughters with his ex-wife, Kirsten Corley, 11-year-old Kensli Bennett and 7-year-old Marli Grace Bennett. The couple were married in 2019 and announced their separation in April 2024, finalizing their divorce in January 2025.

The birth of his third child is not the only big change in Chance’s life lately. During an appearance on Raven-Symoné and Miranda Maday’s Tea Time podcast last month, Chance said that after using it for more than 15 years he’s thinking of switching up his stage name . 

“I think when I first got it, it was just a name that a girl I went to high school with came up with,” Chance told the duo. “I think over time, yes, people would tell me, ‘Yo, you should drop the ‘rapper’ part out of your name because you’re more than rap.’” Chance explained that in the past he has…

items.title: Snubs & Surprises In the 2027 Grammy Nominations
items.summary:
We all knew that the Olivias ( Dean and Rodrigo ) were going to get a lot of love from Grammy voters this year. And sure enough, when nominations for the 69th annual Grammy Awards were announced bright and early on Monday (Nov. 16), they both did. So did such other expected names as Taylor Swift , Bruno Mars and Rosalía .

And it’s hardly a surprise that women dominated the nominations, though the degree of that dominance is impressive. For the first time in Grammy history, the six artists with the most nominations are all women. RAYE leads with 11 nods, followed by Rosalía with nine nods, and then Phoebe Bridgers , Miranda Lambert , Ella Langley and Olivia Rodrigo, with seven each.

But that doesn’t mean there were no surprises in the nominations. It’s impossible to have 100 categories without having at least a few outcomes that don’t land as expected. This year, nearly 16,000 voting members of the Recording Academy were eligible to vote. That includes more than 2,300 new voting members who joined as part of the 2026 new member class.

Final-round voting will take place from Dec. 10 to Jan. 7. The 69th annual Grammy Awards will air on Sunday, Feb. 7, at a new time – 7 p.m. ET/ 4 p.m. PT. The move was designed to let Grammy watchers on the East Coast watch the full show without having to stay up to midnight.

Here are some of the most notable snubs and surprises from the 69th annual Grammy nominations list.
items.t: Snubs & Surprises In the 2027 Grammy Nominations

items.title: RAYE & Rosalía Lead 2027 Grammy Nominations as Women Make History
items.summary:
RAYE is the leading artist in the 2027 Grammy nominations, with 11 nods, tying Beyoncé ’s record set two years ago for the most nods by a woman in one year. But the story goes way beyond RAYE.

For the first time in Grammy history, the six artists with the most nominations are all women. RAYE is followed by Rosalía with nine nods, and then Phoebe Bridgers , Miranda Lambert , Ella Langley and Olivia Rodrigo with seven each. (For the record, the male artists with the most nominations are Bruno Mars and Leon Thomas , with six each.)

Seven of the album of the year nominees are by women artists, which matches the record set in 2024, when the nominees included six female solo artists and one all-female group (boygenius). Three of the same women were nominated in both years: Bridgers (as part of boygenius then; solo now), Rodrigo and Taylor Swift .

items.title: Muse bring a singing robot and ‘The Wow! Signal’ to The O2 in London
items.summary:

The Devonshire space rock trio kicked off their new run and debuted their huge new production in Manchester last week, ahead of their two-night residency in the capital.

The show began with the screens taking the crowd back to August 15, 1977 – the date that a powerful, unexplained 72-second radio burst was detected, originating from the constellation Sagittarius and with its bandwidth and intensity suggesting a possible extraterrestrial source. It became known as ‘The Wow! Signal’. The gig was introduced by frontman Matt Bellamy emerging from floating hexagonal b-stage with laser lights surrounding him for new album highlight ‘Hexagons’, before rejoining his bandmates for the metal-tinged ‘The Sickness In You And I’ and ‘Unravelling’.

The band performed below a giant 3D representation of ‘The Wow! Signal’ waveform forming in space, also seen on the album artwork, and in front of a scene depicting one of Jupiter’s moons, Europa.

items.title: Justice’s ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ score will be the only video game soundtrack the band ever do
items.summary:
Justice have said that their score for Grand Theft Auto 6 will be the only video game soundtrack they ever do.

READ MORE: Every song confirmed for the ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ soundtrack so far 

Last month, Rockstar Games confirmed that dance titans Justice had composed an original score for Grand Theft Auto 6 . So far, two songs from the project have been released –  ‘Flower In A Hurricane’, which features Tame Impala , SZA and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard , and Gesaffelstein collab ‘Pusher’.

The fifty-track, three hour collection will be available to stream December 11 and the record will also be getting a physical release, with a range of vinyl available to pre-order now.

Before that, fans will be able to hear Justice’s music later this week (November 19) when Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases.

In a new interview with French publication Rockyrama , Justice’s Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay have spoken about their decision to work on the highly-anticipated video game.

“When [the offer] arrived on the table, we thought : “If there’s one video game we have to do, it’s this one.” As soon as we accepted and started working [on it], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game,” they said.

According to the band, Rockstar weren’t looking for a specific type of sound or music style for the Grand Theft Auto 6 score. “but rather the emotion that the music should give the player at specific moments.”

They went on to call their Grand Theft Auto 6 score a “special project” but confirmed that they consider it a “real” Justice…
items.t: Justice’s ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ score will be the only video game soundtrack the band ever do

items.summary:

On Sunday night’s (Nov. 15) special edition of The Tonight Show , the singer found the one upside of being home alone: she’s been cranking out new music at an epic pace. “I’m alone, I’m free and I can do whatever the f–k I want,” she told host Jimmy Fallon. “It’s kind of like amazing, but also weird but also amazing.” 

Lopez, 57, said this fall has been the first time since she was in her early 20s that she hasn’t either been with someone or had her kids at home. And while she, of course misses them — one of the twins was actually backstage at the show on Sunday — Lopez said she’s in her “happy era,” explaining that, “When the kids were leaving I was having so many feelings and so many emotions that I went into the studio and started kind of like playing around and making music. items.title: Here Are the 2027 Grammy Nominations in Top Categories: Updating Live
items.summary:
It’s Grammy Nominations morning! The Recording Academy is announcing the nominations for the 69th annual Grammy Awards in all (gulp) 100 categories in a livestream. It’s the first time they’ve done that. In recent years, the academy usually announced the nominations in the six “General Field” categories, and then a representative sample of about 12 more categories. This year they’re going all in.

A roster of past Grammy winners and nominees will help announce the nominees. They include reigning best new artist winner Olivia Dean , who is widely expected to sweep the nominations; Kehlani , who won two Grammys in the R&B field earlier this year; and Amy Allen , who has won songwriter of the year, non-classical the last two years running;

We’ll post the full list of nominees (and much more) the moment the academy announces the last nominee in the last category on the livestream. In the meantime, we’ll show 18 of the biggest categories here as soon as they’re announced.

There’s a reason media focuses on the six “General Field” categories – album, record and song of the year; best new artist; and producer and songwriter of the year, non-classical. Every voting member of the academy (there are currently about 16,000) is permitted to vote in those six categories without using up any of the limited number of categories in which they may vote.

Record, album and song of the year have been presented every year since the first Grammy ceremony in 1959. Best new artist was added for the second ceremony, later in 1959. Producer of the year, non-classical was first presented in 1975.…

items.summary:

READ MORE: Iron Maiden – ‘Senjutsu’ review: an imaginative instant classic 

The British heavy metal icons were finally inducted into the Rock Hall, having formed back in 1975 and been eligible since 2005 – 25 years after their first significant release.

While they weren’t there in person to attend the ceremony on Saturday (November 14) due to touring commitments in Australia, there was a special supergroup that performed at the event to celebrate their huge impact on the metal and rock world.

Jack Black and St. Vincent, came out to perform classic Maiden track ‘The Trooper’, backed by Metallica members Kirk Hammett and Robert Trujillo, Mötley Crüe guitarist John 5, and Rage Against the Machine’s Brad Wilk.

The supergroup was dubbed ‘St. RageTallica 5’, and put their own distinctive spin on the 1983 classic, which was released as part of their fourth studio album, ‘Piece of Mind’. Check it out below.

Jack Black was also on hand to induct the band on the night, sharing a speech on stage and saying: “Has there ever been a band that has rocked this hard for this long? The answer is ‘no.’

“In fact, they’re not even here tonight because they’re rocking half way around the world.”

When it was announced that they were being inducted, the band’s manager shared a statement on their behalf sharing their gratitude. “We’d like to thank the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame for…

items.title: Foo Fighters Announce 2027 U.K. & European Summer Stadium Tour With Support From QOTSA, Iggy Pop & More

Foo Fighters announced a run of U.K. stadium headline performances as part of a European tour in 2027 on Monday (Nov. 16).

The rockers will headline 15 dates across the region, kicking off in Reykjavík, Iceland on June 9. In the U.K., they’ll perform two shows at London’s Wembley Stadium (Sept. 9, 11), alongside dates at The Darlington Arena in Country Durham (Sept. 14), and Edinburgh’s Murrayfield Stadium (Sept. 16). Elsewhere they’ll head to a number of major European cities: Helsinki, Finland; Copenhagen, Denmark; Dusseldorf, Germany; Sofia, Bulgaria; and more dates across the continents. On a number of European dates, they’ll be supported by The Hives, Iggy Pop, Slowdive, Architects and more. See the full run below.

At the U.K. shows they’ll be joined by Garbage (Sept. 9, 16), St. Vincent (Sept. 11, 14), Yard Act (Sept. 14), Florence Road (Sept. 11), Reclus.e (Sept. 9), and The Vaselines (Sept. 16).

Tickets for the U.K. dates will go on sale this Friday (Nov. 20) at 10 a.m. GMT from Gigs and Tours and Ticketmaster .

Foo Fighters last performed in the U.K. earlier this summer with a two-night stand at Liverpool’s Anfield Stadium back in June. The band is currently on the Australian leg of its Take Cover tour, performing at Melbourne’s Marvel Stadium on Saturday night (Nov. 14).

items.title: Johnny Depp’s Hollywood return ‘Ebenezer’ hits top of box office
items.summary:
Johnny Depp ’s Ebenezer is a box office hit despite middling reviews from critics.

Director Ti West’s new take on Charles Dickens’ classic novella A Christmas Carol sees Depp take on the role of Ebenezer Scrooge with Ian McKellen, Rupert Grint and Daisy Ridley also starring.

Ebenezer hit cinemas on Friday (November 13) and across its opening weekend, took a reported $42million worldwide, making it the number one film at the box office. It was the most popular film in UK cinemas, taking $5.4million. Ebenezer also topped the box office in Italy, Mexico, Spain, Poland, Belgium and Central America (via Variety ).

Ahead of its release, Ebenezer received middling reviews from critics and currently has a Rotten Tomatoes score of just 54 per cent. However the response from movie goers has been a lot more positive with Ebenezer racking up a 90 per cent score on the review aggregate site’s fan-voted ‘Popcornmeter’.

Ebenezer is also Johnny Depp’s first major studio movie since 2018’s Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes Of Grindelwald. The same year the Harry Potter prequel was released, Depp’s ex-wife Amber Heard wrote an op-ed for The Washington Post in which she alleged she was domestically abused by the actor

Two years later, Depp lost a libel case in the UK against The Sun for referring to him as a “wife beater” in their reporting and he was asked to resign from the Fantastic Beasts franchise by studio bosses. In 2022, Johnny Depp won a defamation case against Heard in the US which awarded him $10million in compensatory damages and $5million in punitive damages. The jury found that…
items.t: Johnny Depp’s Hollywood return ‘Ebenezer’ hits top of box office

items.title: Peter Hook tells Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame why New Order will never get back together (without Oasis reunion money)
items.summary:
Peter Hook has shut down hopes of a New Order reunion while at the Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame, and said that it would have to be an amount of money similar to what Oasis were offered to make him reconsider.

READ MORE: “It felt like we were changing the world”: inside New Order’s seminal ‘Power, Corruption & Lies’ 

The bassist attended the Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame ceremony on Saturday (November 14) as Joy Division and New Order were inducted together. He appeared at the event without any of the other bandmates present, and performed ‘Love Will Tear Us Apart’ and ‘Bizarre Love Triangle’ alongside Deftones and Chvrches .

Stephen Morris and Gillian Gilbert both did not attend due to health reasons, with Gilbert battling cancer.   Bernard Sumner did not show up on the night either.

Hook played with Joy Division until they became New Order when Ian Curtis took his own life in 1980, before parting ways with the band in 2007 – leading to years of legal battle and trading barbs. There was longstanding tension between some of the other members when he left the band, and he also cited dissatisfaction about the creative direction of the band when he left. New Order went on to tour and record without the bassist, while Peter Hook & The Light have spent years touring to celebrate the discographies of both bands.

He also spoke about financial disputes in an interview with York Calling last year, claiming that he “only earns one penny for every pound the group makes in royalties” despite big contributions to the music, and called it “the utmost treachery”. That interview also saw him…
items.t: Peter Hook tells Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame why New Order will never get back together (without Oasis reunion money)

Westlife are coming to America.

The beloved Irish pop group will extend their Westlife 25: The Anniversary World Tour with a 12-show run across the United States and Canada next March, Billboard can exclusively reveal.

Announced today, the North America trek will get underway March 1, 2027 at YouTube Theater in Inglewood, CA, then visits San Francisco, Edmonton, Calgary, Vancouver, Uncasville, Boston, Orlando, Irving, Toronto, Rosemont, and comes to a halt March 19 at Madison Square Garden in New York City.

It’s just the second tour of North America for the Irish lads, following a sold-out trek in 2024 which included Manhattan’s Radio City Music Hall. 

This next trek, however, promises to dwarf what came before it.

“This is probably one of the most exciting moments of our whole career,” Kian Egan tells Billboard over a Zoom from Paris on Sunday (Nov. 14), just prior to their first-ever performance at the Zenith. Indeed, their first ever performance in the French capital. “Madison Square Garden was always a dream that we thought was probably not in reach for us, because we never really broke the States.” Because of the success of the last tour, the lads dared to dream. “It’s only starting to become real in our minds now,” Egan enthuses.

The date at Allstate Arena in Rosemont, IL will be a particularly special one, landing as it does on St. Patrick’s Day, Wednesday March, 17. “To be Irish boys in our late 40s, bringing people together in Chicago,” says Shane Filan, “that’s just so special to us.” As for playing the Garden, “honestly, it’s mind-blowing. Absolutely…
items.t: Westlife Sets 2027 North America Tour: Exclusive

items.title: Russell Brand still maintains innocence via statement read by wife on podcast
items.summary:
Russell Brand has shared a statement from jail that says he is innocent of rape and sexual assault.

Last week (November 9), Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being found guilty of rape and three counts of sexual assault . During the trial, he was acquitted of two other rape charges and an attempted indecent assault. Throughout the trial, he denied the accusations, saying the incidents had either been consensual, reinvented or re-imagined.

Over the weekend, Brand’s wife Laura Gallacher shared a statement from Brand via the couple’s weekly podcast Sunday Service where the comedian maintains his innocence.

“Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening. The good news is that Christ is with us when we choose him, and I do,” Brand said via Gallacher.

He confirmed that he had been moved to HMP Littlehey, “the biggest sex offenders’ prison in Europe”, but had found the staff “strong, kind, and dedicated.”

“And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone,” he continued. “I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me, let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us.”

Following his conviction, Brand’s former girlfriend Jemima Goldsmith accused him of “violence, coercive control and abuse” while the Met Police have confirmed they’re investigating two more rape allegations against…
items.t: Russell Brand still maintains innocence via statement read by wife on podcast

items.title: Nathan Fielder wasn’t “infatuated” with Elizabeth Holmes while filming ‘You Can See Everything’, says disgraced fraudster’s partner Billy Evans
items.summary:
Billy Evans has debunked rumours that Nathan Fielder was “infatuated” with fraudster Elizabeth Holmes while making his You Can See Everything documentary.

READ MORE: ‘You Can See Everything’ review: a three-hour odyssey of deception, doubt and dodgy dealings 

Holmes was the founder of medical company Theranos who, in the early 2010s, claimed to have revolutionised blood testing. By 2015, Holmes was reportedly the youngest self-made female billionaire in the United States but was accused of deceiving the public over their blood testing claims the same year.

In 2023, she was convicted of defrauding investors and sentenced to 11 years in prison. Along with the company’s former COO Ramesh ‘Sunny’ Balwani, she was also ordered to pay $452million in restitution to victims of the fraud.

Nathan Fielder and Elizabeth Holmes in ‘You Can See Everything’. CREDIT: A24 
 You Can See Everything sees Fielder move in with Holmes and her partner Billy Evans in the weeks leading up to her imprisonment. After a lot of hype , the film launched in cinemas last week and many viewers have been left speculating about the relationship between Fielder and Holmes.

You Can See Everything features a scene where the pair are frolicking in a pool together, and towards the end of the film, someone confronts Fielder about his romantic feelings for Holmes. “Did Nathan grow feelings for Elizabeth?” asks one Reddit post. In a tense interview with CBS News , Evans was asked if he believed Fielder “was in love with your wife?”

“I think a lot of people are infatuated with Elizabeth Holmes,” Evans replied…
items.t: Nathan Fielder wasn’t “infatuated” with Elizabeth Holmes while filming ‘You Can See Everything’, says disgraced fraudster’s partner Billy Evans

items.title: Lily Collins Pays Tribute to Phil Collins After Rock Hall Induction
items.summary:
Lily Collins paid tribute to her father, Phil Collins , following his induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, saying it felt “monumentally special” to stand alongside her family as he accepted the honor.

The Emily in Paris star shared a series of photos from Saturday’s (Nov. 14) ceremony at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater, where Collins was inducted as a solo artist — 16 years after he entered the Hall as a member of Genesis in 2010.

“To see my dad’s extraordinary legacy celebrated with an induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame is something I don’t think I’ll ever quite have the words for,” Lily wrote.

“Seeing you up there on stage embracing all the love, support, and recognition in the room after everything you’ve been through is indescribable,” she continued. “There is no one more deserving. We couldn’t be more proud. I couldn’t be more proud.”

Collins made a rare public appearance at the ceremony, where he was inducted by Travis Barker . He did not perform; Cynthia Erivo sang “In the Air Tonight” in his place, with Barker on drums.

Opening his acceptance speech, Collins told the crowd he’s “really not as bad as it looks,” before making a promise: “You haven’t heard the last of me. I promise you that.”

He went on to thank longtime manager Tony Smith, Atlantic Records’ Ahmet and Nesuhi Ertegun and Virgin Records founder Richard Branson, as well as “my three ex-wives, because they’ve loved me through the years and given me five great children.” He also credited his assistant with saving his life. “I’m not joking when I say without her I wouldn’t be here,” he…
items.t: Lily Collins Pays Tribute to Phil Collins After Rock Hall Induction

items.title: ‘I have to sell my bum on OnlyFans to go on tour’: Kate Nash on fame, feminism and fighting the music business
items.summary:
She threw a (metaphorical) brick through Spotify’s window and exposed industry failings with her ‘Butts for Tour Buses’ campaign. Now the singer is embracing her Irish roots with her new album’s fighting spirit

Kate Nash was standing on a fire truck in a showgirl outfit complete with white tights and pink G-string, shouting through a loudhailer about the music industry’s failure to pay artists fairly, when she wondered if she’d gone too far. It was 2024 and the truck, which made pit stops outside the London offices of Spotify and Live Nation, had a large black-and-white picture of Nash’s bum on the back along with the words “Butts for Tour Buses” – a reference to her newly launched OnlyFans account, which she was using to fund her tour.

That afternoon, she called her manager Kat. “I told her: ‘I’ve thrown a brick through the window at Spotify.’ She went: ‘What, literally?’ and I said: ‘No, but I’ve been standing outside their offices with a megaphone, so that relationship is over. I don’t think we’ll be making their New Music Friday feature.’ And we didn’t.”

items.title: ‘A songbook for protest movements’: how did this secret mission to smuggle antifascist music out of Spain ever get forgotten?
items.summary:
In 1961, a group of Italian creatives crossed the border to collect anti-Franco resistance songs and share them with the world – sparking intense backlash from the dictator. A new documentary retraces that perilous journey

In the summer of 1961, four Italians crossed the Pyrenees into fascist Spain. Unknown to the border guards, their car was loaded with microfilm, a tape recorder and, tucked in the pocket of a writer and musician named Sergio Liberovici, a book of matches – each split in half, etched with the addresses of Spanish antifascists in miniature and glued back together, a hairline fracture concealing secrets that, if discovered, could result in jail or worse.

Along with Michele Luciano Straniero, Emilio Jona and Margherita Galante Garrone, Liberovici was a member of a leftwing collective named Cantacronache. Formed in 1958 and counting Italo Calvino and Umberto Eco among their collaborators, the collective was repulsed by the superficiality of Italian pop music and hoped to revitalise culture with Brechtian realism. At the time, Italy was fiercely divided into leftwing and rightwing political camps, and it was a record label, Italia Canta, linked to the Italian Communist party, that financed the trip. Its goal: to secretly document the resistance songs of the anti-Franco underground. It was a perilous task for all involved, but especially so for Cantacronache’s contacts.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘A songbook for protest movements’: how did this secret mission to smuggle antifascist music out of Spain ever get forgotten?

items.title: Ocean Colour Scene review – no other band of their era can do it like this
items.summary:
Ulster Hall, Belfast
With two sets of fathers and sons now in the group, as they play all of Moseley Shoals on its 30th anniversary, the indie stalwarts have aged into seismic and soulful performers

‘It’s only 30 years ago,” Simon Fowler says of Moseley Shoals. He would seem to mean it, but 30 years makes Ocean Colour Scene’s breakthrough album as old now as Revolver was when they were making it. The band once derided for raiding the 60s are now heritage themselves. They open the album’s anniversary tour on the stage where Led Zeppelin first played Stairway to Heaven, and you can’t help but appreciate the lineage.

They walk on to Green Onions, fresh from the Crown Bar, and open with You’ve Got It Bad, all supreme Motown stomp. Fowler sings with a hand in his pocket and looks taken aback by the welcome. The casualness is a conduit: his voice has aged into something close to peak Joe Cocker, grained at the edges, honey underneath. Lining Your Pockets is more resounding than ever.

Continue reading...

items.title: Paris Paloma review – arena-scale alt-pop drama from a singer on her way to bigger things
items.summary:
Bristol Beacon
The UK artist combines feminist fury with accessible melodies and a dramatic flair that sees her alternately pogoing and seeking out the wind machines at the prow of the stage

People are dancing to a song they don’t know, with flower garlands in their hair and their arms around their friends. This reaction to Fairy Dance, an unreleased track written about the community that has sprung up around her music, says a lot about the moment Paris Paloma finds herself in, and tonight’s show feels for all the world like a stepping stone to bigger things.

Throughout, Paloma leans in to the built-in drama of songs from her second album, The Fatal Flaw, which pairs ornate folk arrangements with the sort of arena-sized alt-pop production favoured by Florence + the Machine. With a sculpture inspired by surrealist Ithell Colquhoun’s Tree of Veins dominating the stage, she falls to her knees to deliver high notes and seeks out wind machines at the prow of the stage, her flowing crimson dress buffeted as if on a wintry moor.

Continue reading...

items.title: James Blunt: ‘Do I have a nickname? Yes, it rhymes with blunt’
items.summary:
The singer on his love for Ibiza, the weirdest thing he’s done in the name of romance, and being signed up for Celebrity Traitors against his will

You were a punching bag for such a long time after You’re Beautiful became a massive hit but your consistent good humour is deeply admirable. Does it ever get tiring?

It was a surprise, at the beginning. I was just a little guy with a dream. And when you achieve your dream, you think people would be happy for you. For them not to be happy for you but angry with you, for your song, seems irrational, an overreaction. It is interesting how people generally want to tear people down for achieving their little dreams. But I’d had a real proper job before that [as a captain in the British army]. My friends might have been on operations in Afghanistan or Iraq, so if I were to complain to them at the time saying, “Oh, the Guardian said something really horrid about me and gave me three stars for my album” – they would be able to talk about who had lost their lives or limbs that day, and that put it all in perspective. And perspective is everything.

Continue reading...
items.t: James Blunt: ‘Do I have a nickname? Yes, it rhymes with blunt’

items.title: ‘Young, Black and female in Brixton is hard’: ​from football to Top Boy and wordplay, the inspiring journey of UK rapper Cristale
items.summary:
Crystal Palace FC or Oxbridge beckoned, but the multitalented MC kept forging her way towards music. She explains how she poured every aspect of herself into her debut mixtape

Two weeks before we meet, UK rapper Cristale was scrambling down a cliff face to a secluded black pebbled beach in Dover, racing an incoming tide with fewer than 90 minutes to shoot the video for her single I’m Okay With Being Lonely. She’d never hiked before in her life. “I was wearing head-to-toe Stone Island, no hiking gear, full face of makeup, edges laid and Mum was doing my touch-ups on a rusty ladder,” she laughs.

As we sit in her publicist’s central London office, her hair half-braided and half-flowing past a black puffer coat, she says the rush of adrenaline hasn’t fully faded. In fact she seems to thrive on regular bumps of it: beyond her relentlessly articulate and energetic rap flow – put to work on tracks that span drill, introspective R&B and beyond – she has ably hopped between football, art, acting in Netflix projects and more.
